summary.description: Two sentences on what this section is doing well and where it is weakest, written to the author.

findings.description: One entry per place worth changing, strongest first. Return [] when the section needs nothing.

selectedText.description: Exact, uniquely occurring text from the source that this finding is about, copied character for character including LaTeX markup. Anchor the smallest span that contains the problem.

level.description: argument: what the section claims or the order it claims it in. paragraph: what a paragraph is for and how it opens or closes. sentence: structure inside one sentence. wording: a term or phrase.

principle.description: The reading principle at stake, in plain words. For example: the new information is not in the stress position; the paragraph opens on something the reader has no context for; the action is buried in a noun.

issue.description: What a reader loses here, stated concretely. Not a restatement of the principle.

suggestion.description: What to do about it, written as an instruction the author could hand back as a comment.
